title: 隆慶四年貴州武舉鄉試錄
text:
貴州武舉錄序
隆慶庚午秋侍御蔡公既登
進文學士與計偕矣冬十月
復當校武士乃申飭諸故事
下所司舉行如
制於是檄鳴臣與右叅議林澄
源提調其事而監試以屬副
===
使秦淦惟時諸衛武胄暨列
郡良家子挾矢抱策者咸踴
躍翔集侍御公乃率大小諸
執事韋諸待試者于轅門下
按規布鵠始令馳而射次步
而射進其不詭于式者就棘
院考策論已乃校其儁十有
punctuated:
貴州武舉錄序

隆慶庚午秋，侍御蔡公既登進文學士與計偕矣。冬十月，復當校武士，乃申飭諸故事，下所司舉行如制。於是檄鳴臣與右叅議林澄源提調其事，而監試以屬副使秦淦。惟時諸衛武胄暨列郡良家子，挾矢抱策者，咸踴躍翔集。侍御公乃率大小諸執事，韋諸待試者于轅門下，按規布鵠，始令馳而射，次步而射，進其不詭于式者就棘院考策論。已乃校其儁十有
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guizhou Military Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the gengwu year of Longqing [1570], Censor Cai had already selected and advanced the civil candidates to travel to the capital with the tribute mission. In winter, in the tenth month, it was again time to examine military candidates. He therefore reiterated the established procedures and directed the responsible offices to carry them out in accordance with the regulations. He thereupon issued instructions appointing me, Mingchen, and Right Administration Assistant Lin Chengyuan as Proctors for the examination, while entrusting its supervision to Surveillance Vice Commissioner Qin Gan.

At this time, descendants of military families from the various guards, together with sons of respectable families from the several prefectures, came bearing arrows and written policy essays, all eagerly gathering from every direction. The Censor then led the senior and junior functionaries and assembled [?] the candidates awaiting examination below the headquarters gate. Targets were set out according to the prescribed rules. First he ordered the candidates to shoot while riding, then to shoot on foot. Those whose performance conformed to the prescribed standards were advanced to the examination compound to be tested in policy essays and discourses. title: 隆慶四年貴州武舉鄉試錄
text:
八人刻其姓名與文爲錄鳴
臣當一言序諸首簡序曰夫
自古國家際盈成之運雖治
極熙洽而未始不以武備爲
意蓋所以振揚國威固護元
氣制治保邦有不容或緩者
觀之成周制禮作樂以致太
===
平而張皇之訓不敢少懈於
四方無虞之日至於農隙則
講蒐田以共武服賔興則兼
射御以論秀士當其時雖未
立武科而奔走禦侮之臣干
城腹心之寄濟濟克生寔稱
任使王國賴之故有周順治
punctuated: 八人，刻其姓名與文爲錄。鳴臣當一言序諸首簡。序曰：夫自古國家際盈成之運，雖治極熙洽，而未始不以武備爲意，蓋所以振揚國威，固護元氣，制治保邦，有不容或緩者。觀之成周，制禮作樂以致太平，而張皇之訓，不敢少懈於四方無虞之日。至於農隙，則講蒐田以共武服；賔興，則兼射御以論秀士。當其時，雖未立武科，而奔走禦侮之臣，干城腹心之寄，濟濟克生，寔稱任使，王國賴之。故有周順治
translation_en:
…eight men, whose names and essays were engraved for publication as a record. I, Mingchen [?], was charged with supplying a few words of preface for its opening pages. The preface reads:
From antiquity, whenever a state enjoyed an age of full prosperity, even when its government had attained the utmost harmony, it never ceased to attend to military preparedness. For this served to display the state’s might, safeguard its vital strength, establish good government, and preserve the realm—matters that could brook no delay. Consider the Zhou: they instituted rites and composed music to bring about great peace, yet even when the four quarters were free from danger, they dared not relax in the slightest their injunctions to maintain martial vigor. During breaks in agricultural work, they practiced seasonal hunts to prepare for military service; when honoring and recommending worthy men, they also assessed archery and charioteering in judging outstanding candidates. Although no military examination category had yet been established, servants who hastened to repel aggression, men entrusted to serve as the realm’s shield and rampart and as its intimate confidants, arose in abundance. They were truly equal to their appointments and duties, and the kingdom relied upon them. Thus the Zhou’s orderly government…

title: 隆慶四年貴州武舉鄉試錄
text:
威嚴之烈垂之彌久而迄今
頌得人之盛不衰我
國家酌古定制中外衛所之設
星連棊布武弁蓋已稱盛復
立武舉專科三歲論之於鄉
而升之於大司馬此其制視
成周加詳矣
===
皇上聖神撫運
龍飛之始首舉大閱
鴻威丕振頃又
俞言者之請屢詔中外搜羅將材
以
聞
聖謨睿慮宏而且遠其殆安不忘
punctuated:
威嚴之烈，垂之彌久，而迄今頌得人之盛不衰。我國家酌古定制，中外衛所之設，星連棊布，武弁蓋已稱盛。復立武舉專科，三歲論之於鄉，而升之於大司馬，此其制視成周加詳矣。
皇上聖神撫運，龍飛之始，首舉大閱，鴻威丕振。頃又俞言者之請，屢詔中外搜羅將材以聞。聖謨睿慮，宏而且遠，其殆安不忘
translation_en:
…the achievements of its imposing might have endured ever longer, and even now praise for its abundant recruitment of worthy men has not diminished. Our dynasty has weighed ancient precedents and established its institutions. Its guards and battalions, within the capital and beyond, are arrayed like stars and distributed like pieces on a chessboard; its military officers may already be called numerous. It has further established a separate military examination, assessing candidates every three years in the provinces and advancing them to the Minister of War. Compared with that of the Zhou, this system is still more fully elaborated.
His Majesty, sagely and divinely discerning, presides over the fortunes of the age. At the very beginning of his accession, he first held a grand military review, greatly displaying his majestic might. Recently, he also approved a proposal submitted to him and repeatedly commanded officials within the capital and beyond to seek out men with talent for command and report them to the throne. His sagely plans and discerning deliberations are broad and far-reaching. Surely these express a heart that, in security, does not forget…

title: 隆慶四年貴州武舉鄉試錄
text:
危之心乎斯與詰兵揚烈�London
鞈講武者又奚殊焉夫豪傑
振世之才未甞乏於天下然
惟草昧開創之初士多雲合
景從卽鼓刀販繒之徒往往
積功閥位通侯比至承平介
胄文墨與時恬嬉一旦猝有
===
烽燧之警亡論紈綺驕穉不
足倚賴卽㮴之草澤求所謂
鷹揚敵愾之士益難其人蓋
時平習玩乃自古嘆之矣然
則有國者之需將不蓄之於
豫可乎方今寰寓乂安號稱
極治固無山海窺竊之虞也
punctuated: 危之心乎？斯與詰兵揚烈�London鞈講武者，又奚殊焉？夫豪傑振世之才，未甞乏於天下，然惟草昧開創之初，士多雲合景從，卽鼓刀販繒之徒，往往積功閥，位通侯。比至承平，介胄文墨與時恬嬉，一旦猝有烽燧之警，亡論紈綺驕穉不足倚賴，卽㮴之草澤，求所謂鷹揚敵愾之士，益難其人。蓋時平習玩，乃自古嘆之矣。然則有國者之需將，不蓄之於豫可乎？方今寰寓乂安，號稱極治，固無山海窺竊之虞也。
translation_en: …a concern for danger? How does this differ from putting the troops in order, displaying martial prowess, and conducting military training [?]? The world has never lacked outstanding men with talents capable of stirring their age. Yet it is chiefly in the unsettled beginnings of a dynasty that such men gather like clouds and follow like shadows. Even those who wield a butcher’s knife or sell silk often accumulate meritorious achievements and attain the rank of marquis. Once lasting peace arrives, however, military men and civil officials alike grow complacent and idle with the times. Should a sudden alarm arise from the beacon fires, not only are pampered youths in fine silks unfit to be relied upon, but even searching [?] among men in the countryside makes it all the harder to find those who soar like hawks and bear resolute hostility toward the enemy. Indeed, the complacency bred by peaceful times has been lamented since antiquity. Since rulers need commanders, can they afford not to cultivate a reserve of them beforehand? Today, all within the realm is peaceful and well governed, in what is acclaimed as an age of consummate order. Certainly there is no fear of hostile forces from the mountains or seas seeking an opportunity to seize our territory.

title: 隆慶四年貴州武舉鄉試錄
text:
而將材之儲則不可一日不
講者譬之攝生之家芝苓之
屬固無不具而烏雄酷烈亦
未始以其不用而不之蓄彼
誠不欲其卒爾而無備也然
則今日武科之舉侍御公正
以仰承
===
皇上飭武簡賢之至意而汲汲乎
必欲得眞才而進之也貴雖
僻在荒徼人才之生不以地
限豈無請纓投筆者出於其
間足以仰副
當宁樹闢之思者乎今夫行空之
駿稱良矣使鹽車終困則一
punctuated: 而將材之儲，則不可一日不講者。譬之攝生之家，芝苓之屬固無不具，而烏雄酷烈，亦未始以其不用而不之蓄。彼誠不欲其卒爾而無備也。然則今日武科之舉，侍御公正以仰承皇上飭武簡賢之至意，而汲汲乎必欲得眞才而進之也。貴雖僻在荒徼，人才之生不以地限，豈無請纓投筆者出於其間，足以仰副當宁樹闢之思者乎？今夫行空之駿，稱良矣；使鹽車終困，則一
translation_en:
…Yet the cultivation of a reserve of military talent must not be neglected for even a single day. Consider a household devoted to preserving health: it keeps a full supply of such things as lingzhi and poria, but also stocks potent, harsh substances such as aconite and realgar, even when it has no use for them. It truly wishes to avoid being caught unprepared by a sudden emergency. Thus, in conducting the military examination today, His Honor the Censor is carrying out His Majesty’s earnest intention to put military affairs in order and select worthy men, eagerly determined to find and advance genuine talent.

Although Guizhou lies remotely on the wild frontier, the emergence of talent is not bounded by geography. Could there not arise among its people men who volunteer for service or lay aside the writing brush to take up arms, capable of fulfilling the reigning sovereign’s aspirations to establish and expand his rule [?]? title: 隆慶四年貴州武舉鄉試錄
text:
瞬千里之步不顯士負泛駕
跅弛之材設無青雲之媒則
龐眉不免興嗟何則遇固有
不易也諸士今既逢機遘會
登名夏官效用有階視向之
竄伏窮荒草莽間至殊絕矣
所以攄奇出慮以報荅今日
===
之隆遇者則何以哉夫弓馬
策論末技也不足言才所謂
眞才在忠以狥國能樹勤勞
於社稷耳古今登壇推轂之
士以武科進者豈少乎而獨
郭汾陽岳武穆稱爲得人彼
其忠貫日月功垂宗社國家
punctuated: 瞬千里之步不顯。士負泛駕跅弛之材，設無青雲之媒，則龐眉不免興嗟。何則？遇固有不易也。諸士今既逢機遘會，登名夏官，效用有階，視向之竄伏窮荒草莽間，至殊絕矣。所以攄奇出慮，以報荅今日之隆遇者，則何以哉？夫弓馬策論，末技也，不足言才。所謂眞才，在忠以狥國，能樹勤勞於社稷耳。古今登壇推轂之士，以武科進者豈少乎？而獨郭汾陽、岳武穆稱爲得人。彼其忠貫日月，功垂宗社，國家
translation_en:
…its stride, capable of covering a thousand li in an instant, remains unmanifest. A man may possess exceptional talent that chafes at restraint, but without a patron to help him rise into the azure clouds, he cannot avoid sighing in disappointment even when his eyebrows have grown shaggy with age. Why is this? A favorable opportunity is indeed difficult to obtain. You gentlemen have now encountered such an opportunity: your names are registered with the Ministry of War, and you have a means of entering service. Your circumstances are utterly different from when you lay hidden among the wilds of this remote frontier. How, then, will you bring forth your exceptional abilities and devise plans to repay the generous recognition you have received today?

Archery, horsemanship, policy essays, and discourses are merely subsidiary skills, insufficient in themselves to constitute talent. True talent lies in loyalty that dedicates itself to the state, and in rendering meritorious service to the altars of soil and grain. Among those throughout history who have ascended the commander's platform and been dispatched with command of armies, have there been few who advanced through the military examinations? Yet Guo Fenyang 郭汾陽 [Guo Ziyi] and Yue Wumu 岳武穆 [Yue Fei] alone are singled out as instances of finding the right men. Their loyalty reached the sun and moon, and their achievements bestowed lasting benefits upon the ancestral temples and the altars of the state. The state's…

title: 隆慶四年貴州武舉鄉試錄
text:
之安危實係之其才蓋匪區區
區技藝已也今多士直以弓
矢策論舉耳其忠義之悃未
之或知假令進而任疆埸當
韜鈐之寄果能決策宣猷殫
智畢力無事則秉義奉公而
不私其身圖有事則奮軀捍
===
難而弗怵於利害策勳效節
期媲美於汾陽武穆焉如是
則可庶幾於周室禦侮干城
之佐而無負
國家養士育材之恩其於今日
奮武保邦之圖不爲無助矣
如其急於私計緩於王事忠
punctuated: 之安危實係之，其才蓋匪區區區技藝已也。今多士直以弓矢策論舉耳，其忠義之悃未之或知。假令進而任疆埸，當韜鈐之寄，果能決策宣猷，殫智畢力，無事則秉義奉公而不私其身圖，有事則奮軀捍難而弗怵於利害，策勳效節，期媲美於汾陽、武穆焉。如是，則可庶幾於周室禦侮干城之佐，而無負國家養士育材之恩，其於今日奮武保邦之圖不爲無助矣。如其急於私計，緩於王事，忠
translation_en:
…its safety or peril truly depended upon them; their abilities surely amounted to more than mere technical skills [the transcription repeats 區]. Now you candidates have been selected solely on the basis of archery, policy essays, and discourses; the sincerity of your loyalty and righteousness remains unknown. Suppose you advance to service on the frontiers and are entrusted with military command: can you indeed determine strategy and carry out sound plans, exhausting your wisdom and exerting all your strength? In peaceful times, can you uphold righteousness and serve the public without pursuing schemes for your own benefit [?]; and in times of trouble, can you throw yourselves into warding off danger, undeterred by considerations of gain or harm, earning merit and demonstrating fidelity, aspiring to match Fenyang and Wumu?
If so, you may approach the standard of those servants of the Zhou royal house who resisted aggression and served as its shield and wall, and you will not betray the state's beneficence in nurturing scholars and fostering talent. You will thus contribute to today's undertaking of strengthening military prowess and safeguarding the realm. But if you attend urgently to private schemes and only slowly to royal service, your loyalty…

title: 隆慶四年貴州武舉鄉試錄
text:
款無閒卽今穿楊貫蝨謀孫
吳而智韓白國家又將焉用
之多士僉侍御公求得眞才
之意其尚知所懋哉
貴州等處承宣布政使司左
叅政王鳴臣謹序
punctuated:
款無閒，卽今穿楊貫蝨，謀孫吳而智韓白，國家又將焉用之？多士僉侍御公求得眞才之意，其尚知所懋哉！
貴州等處承宣布政使司左叅政王鳴臣謹序。
translation_en:
…with unremitting sincerity [?], even if they can now pierce a willow leaf or shoot through a louse, devise strategies like Sun Wu and Wu Qi, and display the wisdom of Han Xin and Bai Qi, what use would the state have for them? May all you candidates understand the censor’s intention to obtain truly talented men [?] and recognize what you should strive toward!
Preface respectfully composed by Wang Mingchen, Left Administration Vice Commissioner of the Guizhou Provincial Administration Commission.

title: 隆慶四年貴州武舉鄉試錄

武舉鄉試條格

巡按貴州監察御史蔡，爲武舉事，奉都察院巡按貴州柒千伍百伍拾玖號勘合劄付，准兵部咨：「該本部題，職方清吏司案呈：『照得隆慶肆年，例該天下開科武舉鄉試，欲預行都察院幷南京兵部、各處巡撫都御史及浙江等布政司、順天應天貳府，各照本部前科會官題准事例，依期開科鄉試。』案呈到部，看得武舉試期不遠，相應預舉，合候命下，本部備將歷科武舉鄉試條格，通行各該衙門，依期遵照舉行等因。隆慶肆年貳月初壹日，本部尚書霍等具題，初叁日奉聖旨：『是。』欽此。欽遵，擬合通行，爲此合咨貴院，煩爲轉行各該巡按監察御史，查照本部題奉欽依内事理，欽遵施行。」等因到院。准此，擬合通行，爲此合行劄仰本職依奉查照施行。奉
translation_en:
Regulations for the Military Provincial Examination

Cai, Investigating Censor serving as Regional Inspector of Guizhou, on the matter of the military examinations, received a tally-authenticated directive from the Censorate, numbered 7,559 in the Guizhou Regional Inspection series. It conveyed the following communication from the Ministry of War:

“This Ministry submitted a memorial based on a report from the Bureau of Military Operations: ‘Under the established rules, military Provincial Examinations are to be held throughout the empire in the fourth year of Longqing [1570]. We propose to notify in advance the Censorate, the Nanjing Ministry of War, the Censors-in-chief serving as Grand Coordinators in the various regions, the Provincial Administration Commissions of Zhejiang and the other provinces, and the two prefectures of Shuntian and Yingtian. Each shall hold the Provincial Examination at the prescribed time, following the precedents jointly memorialized by this Ministry and the assembled officials and approved by the throne for the preceding examination.’

“Upon receiving this report, the Ministry considered that the military examination date was approaching and that preparations should accordingly be made in advance. Once the imperial command was issued, this Ministry should circulate the complete regulations for military Provincial Examinations from successive examination sessions to all the offices concerned, for observance and implementation at the prescribed time.

“On the first day of the second month of the fourth year of Longqing, Huo, Minister of War, and the other officials of this Ministry submitted the memorial. On the third day, they received the imperial rescript: ‘Approved.’ Reverently received. In reverent obedience, we propose that notification be circulated. We therefore address this communication to your Censorate, requesting that you transmit it to the Investigating Censors serving as Regional Inspectors concerned, so that they may examine the provisions in this Ministry’s imperially approved memorial and reverently carry them out.”

The policy question may draw upon ancient military methods or ask about current affairs. It need not rely exclusively on conventional statements found in books, merely rewarding memorization and thereby overlooking genuine talent. Those who were previously dispatched to the Ministry for the joint examination but failed, and who now come again for the Metropolitan Examination, shall be permitted to undergo assessment and be dispatched on the same basis as the others. Assessment and selection shall comprise five grades, all following the military Metropolitan Examination procedure. The guards and battalions in the two capitals shall recommend and forward candidates under guarantee; the respective Chief Military Commissions shall forward them in consolidated groups to the Central Chief Military Commission. The Ten Upper Guards and the military schools shall recommend and forward candidates directly to the Central Chief Military Commission. For each candidate recommended by a guard or battalion, a clear statement must be supplied concerning his customary resourcefulness and courage, his training in riding, archery, and military methods, and his having never been judicially sentenced and dispatched for punishment [?]. These statements, together with the assessments from the respective places, shall accompany the candidates when they are sent. The same applies to candidates recommended by commissions, prefectures, subprefectures, counties, guards, and battalions outside the capitals.

中之人行令該府量資盤費給文
起送到部本部於會試之年照例
於武舉場事畢日將前送到武生

者發回肄業中者不必分等止將

In such cases, only those who are indeed exceptional may be formally referred to the prefecture concerned. Only after the prefect of the originating prefecture [?] has examined and approved them may they be presented to the Regional Inspector. Those selected by the Regional Inspector shall, as appropriate, receive the robes and caps of military students and be enrolled as such, with exemption from miscellaneous labor services. In an examination year, each prefecture shall issue documents and send them together to the Regional Inspector. Those proficient in discourses and policy essays shall enter the examination compound with the military examination candidates as before. All the others shall wait until the military examination has concluded, when the Regional Inspector shall examine them jointly with the other officials concerned. Those outstanding in both intelligence and courage shall be placed in the first class; those proficient in a single skill shall be placed in the second class. Each shall receive the preferential treatment accorded to military examination candidates. The poorest performers shall be sent back to their places of registration to perform labor services.

title: 隆慶四年貴州武舉鄉試錄
text:
分發京營幷各邊立爲教師名色
即充隊長教練各軍俱許隨軍食
糧差操三年之間獲有功次挨陞
職級如無功級但係訓練有成教
師即補把總把總即補千總月加
米壹石與武舉一體保薦推用如
或在營教練無成不肯向上者聽
督撫官徑自革回起送之時各府
州縣如敢徇情濫送聽巡按御史
===
指實糾治等因奉
聖旨是這武生你每會同監察御史驗果有勇
力技能的咨送薊鎮軍門再行覈實徑自去
留京營及各邊俱不必發去欽此
punctuated: 分發京營幷各邊，立爲教師名色，即充隊長，教練各軍，俱許隨軍食糧。差操三年之間，獲有功次，挨陞職級；如無功級，但係訓練有成，教師即補把總，把總即補千總，月加米壹石，與武舉一體保薦推用。如或在營教練無成、不肯向上者，聽督撫官徑自革回。起送之時，各府州縣如敢徇情濫送，聽巡按御史指實糾治。等因，奉聖旨：「是。這武生，你每會同監察御史驗，果有勇力技能的，咨送薊鎮軍門，再行覈實，徑自去留。京營及各邊俱不必發去。」欽此。
translation_en:
…to be distributed among the capital garrisons and the various frontier commands, given the designation of instructor, and assigned as squad leaders to train the troops. All shall be permitted to draw grain rations with the troops. During three years of service and drill, those who earn merit shall be promoted through the ranks in due order. Those who have earned no merit qualifying them for advancement but have achieved results in training shall nevertheless receive appointments: instructors as company commanders (bazong), and company commanders as battalion commanders (qianzong). They shall receive an additional one shi of rice monthly and shall be recommended and selected for employment on the same basis as military provincial graduates. Those who achieve no results in training at their garrisons and are unwilling to improve may be dismissed and sent home directly by the supreme commanders and grand coordinators. When sending candidates forward, if any prefectural, subprefectural, or county authorities dare to favor personal connections and send unqualified men indiscriminately, the Regional Inspector shall identify the specific offenses and impeach those responsible for punishment.
A submission to this effect received the imperial rescript: “Approved. You shall examine these military students jointly with the Investigating Censor. Those who truly possess courage, strength, skills, and abilities shall be referred by official communication to the military headquarters of Jizhen for further verification, and that headquarters shall decide directly whether to dismiss or retain them. There is no need to dispatch any to the capital garrisons or the various frontier commands.” Respect this.

The barrel should be long, its bore straight, its dimensions uniform, and its walls of even thickness; the gunpowder mixture should be fine, and those using the weapons should be practiced in their use. Not one of these six requirements may be neglected. Yet weapons made of iron readily deteriorate [?] over time, while those made of copper readily soften when fired. What must be done to make them satisfactory? Some say that when deploying these weapons against an enemy, the troops should form three ranks: the front rank should be narrow and the rear rank broad, with the rear twice the size of the middle and the middle twice the size of the front. What precisely is the reasoning behind this? Some say that unless the central formation is firm, the front rank will lack steadfast resolve, and that unless the commanding general has discernment, the use of firearms will achieve no success. Are firearms indeed insufficient to rely upon? Some say that on the northern frontier, where open country stretches a thousand li and bowmen number in the tens of thousands, troops do not form orderly ranks, and blades have already crossed before firearms can be brought into action. Does this mean that firearms cannot be used against the northern barbarians? Some say that the victories over the southwestern barbarians at the founding of the dynasty were achieved through the use of firearms. Now, however, enforcement of laws and orders has grown somewhat lax. Even if the major frontier garrisons earnestly wish to manufacture these weapons and train in their use, there is fear that unscrupulous merchants, through cross-border trade, will instead put them into the enemy’s hands. Does this mean that training with firearms is also inadvisable in the southwest? Establishing a system and putting it into practice is what is called method; applying it with inspired understanding rests with the individual. If we now wish to use China’s superior skills to chastise the barbarians of the four quarters, with success wherever they are employed, there must surely be a way to do so. Let you candidates analyze these matters, determine the soundest judgment, and reply.

Comment by Examiner Shen, Prefect: “Those who discuss warfare, past and present, concern themselves with no more than the two methods of attack and defense. Yet emptiness and substance, outward dispositions and displays, cannot be governed by fixed rules. This essay repeatedly examines and debates attack and defense, revealing a subtle grasp of their application. When he faces battle in the future, he will surely have a winning strategy.”

Warfare has outward dispositions: use emptiness to display substance, and the actions undertaken on our side will not exhaust us. Warfare has pivotal opportunities: conceal substance within emptiness, and the means by which we control the enemy will secure victory. Now, when we use emptiness to display substance, all our apparent substance is empty. The enemy will certainly follow it, while ease remains always on our side. If we prevail, the enemy does not.

之畫以決其策多爲之說以濟其變而深
沉要妙孫吳其最也愚嘗極其要歸而論
之不越乎攻與守而已夫攻守者法也可
得而言也出於法之外者攻守之妙用也
===
不可得而言也法如四序之有寒暑二氣
之有剛柔一定而不可易不必明者而後
可以依據其迹也出於法之外者如寒暑
之有推遷剛柔之有摩盪運用而不可窮
非至明者無以擬議其變也昔漢太醫令
淳于意能診病決人死生文帝問意曰子
治病能全無失乎意對曰意治病人必先
切其脉乃治之逆者不可治其順者乃治
之不能全無失也嗚呼彼所謂良醫也而
punctuated:
備，我得以其實乘敵之虛焉，而實者有全功矣。微乎！神乎！此兵事之極詭，而古之賢將所以動而勝人，功烈著於當時，名聲垂而不泯者，未嘗不以是道也。
今夫武經一書，古哲人智士出其獨得之見，往往預爲之畫以決其策，多爲之說以濟其變，而深沉要妙，孫吳其最也。愚嘗極其要歸而論之，不越乎攻與守而已。夫攻守者，法也，可得而言也；出於法之外者，攻守之妙用也，不可得而言也。法如四序之有寒暑，二氣之有剛柔，一定而不可易，不必明者而後可以依據其迹也。出於法之外者，如寒暑之有推遷，剛柔之有摩盪，運用而不可窮，非至明者無以擬議其變也。
昔漢太醫令淳于意能診病決人死生。文帝問意曰：「子治病能全無失乎？」意對曰：「意治病人，必先切其脉乃治之。逆者不可治，其順者乃治之，不能全無失也。」嗚呼！彼所謂良醫也，而
translation_en:
…preparations, I can use my actual strength to exploit the enemy’s weakness, and thereby achieve complete success through that strength. How subtle! How wondrous! This is the utmost artifice of warfare. When worthy generals of antiquity acted and defeated others, winning achievements illustrious in their own times and leaving names that endured without fading, they invariably did so through this Way.
Now, in the Military Classics, wise and discerning men of antiquity set forth their distinctive insights. They often devised plans in advance to settle their strategies and offered extensive explanations to meet changing circumstances. For depth, essential insight, and subtlety, Sunzi and Wuzi are foremost among them. I have ventured to examine their ultimate purport and conclude that it extends no further than attack and defense. Attack and defense are methods that can be expressed in words; what lies beyond those methods is the subtle application of attack and defense, which cannot be expressed in words. Methods resemble the cold and heat of the four seasons, or the hardness and softness of the two vital forces: they are fixed and unalterable. One need not possess exceptional discernment to follow their established patterns. What lies beyond methods resembles the shifting of cold and heat and the mutual interplay of hardness and softness: its applications are inexhaustible. Without the highest discernment, one cannot fathom its transformations.
In the past, Chunyu Yi, Director of the Imperial Medical Office under the Han, could diagnose illness and determine whether a person would live or die. Emperor Wen asked him, “When you treat illnesses, can you avoid all failures?” Yi replied, “When I treat a sick person, I must first feel the pulse before proceeding with treatment. Those whose signs are adverse cannot be treated; I treat those whose signs are favorable. I cannot avoid all failures.” Alas! He was what is called a skilled physician, yet…

title: 隆慶四年貴州武舉鄉試錄
text:
順逆云者果得於方乎抑不得於方乎知
醫之不可泥於方則知兵之不可泥於經
矣是故不達於攻守之形者知實而不知
虛也敵且以其實角我焉而吾實窮於已
矣不達於攻守之機者知虛而不知實也
敵且以其虛嘗我焉而吾虛聞於人矣實
窮於已譬則開戶以待乘垣之盜弩張弦
絕而莫之繼者也虛聞於人譬則閉戶以
卻斬關之盜弩弛矢逸而莫之禦者也其
===
無救於覆亡之禍均焉吾以妙於虛實之
用者言之攻其可勝守其不可勝而度其
有餘不足之分則人己審矣攻所不守守
所不攻而先爲不可勝以待之則先後權
矣攻心爲上攻城爲下守氣爲上守城爲
下則攻守有其要矣守以出乎攻攻以存
乎守則攻守互爲用矣吾智藏於九地之
下忽而往敵莫循其所由往吾兵動於九
天之上忽而來敵莫窺其所自來利以誘
punctuated:
順逆云者，果得於方乎？抑不得於方乎？知醫之不可泥於方，則知兵之不可泥於經矣。是故不達於攻守之形者，知實而不知虛也。敵且以其實角我焉，而吾實窮於已矣。不達於攻守之機者，知虛而不知實也。敵且以其虛嘗我焉，而吾虛聞於人矣。實窮於已，譬則開戶以待乘垣之盜，弩張弦絕而莫之繼者也；虛聞於人，譬則閉戶以卻斬關之盜，弩弛矢逸而莫之禦者也。其無救於覆亡之禍均焉。
吾以妙於虛實之用者言之：攻其可勝，守其不可勝，而度其有餘不足之分，則人己審矣；攻所不守，守所不攻，而先爲不可勝以待之，則先後權矣；攻心爲上，攻城爲下，守氣爲上，守城爲下，則攻守有其要矣；守以出乎攻，攻以存乎守，則攻守互爲用矣。吾智藏於九地之下，忽而往，敵莫循其所由往；吾兵動於九天之上，忽而來，敵莫窺其所自來。利以誘
translation_en:
…As for what he called favorable and adverse conditions, were these discerned through prescribed methods, or apart from them? Once we understand that medicine cannot adhere rigidly to prescriptions, we understand that warfare cannot adhere rigidly to the classics. Thus, one who fails to comprehend the configurations of attack and defense knows strength but not weakness. The enemy will pit his strength against us, and our own strength will be exhausted. One who fails to comprehend the critical opportunities for attack and defense knows weakness but not strength. The enemy will probe us with a show of weakness, and our weakness will become known to others. To exhaust our own strength is like opening the door to await thieves who scale the wall: the crossbow is drawn, its string snaps, and there is nothing to follow it up. To let our weakness become known to others is like shutting the door to repel thieves who break through the gate: the crossbow goes slack, the bolt flies astray, and there is nothing to ward them off. Both alike leave us without remedy against the disaster of defeat and destruction.
Let me speak of those who are masterful in employing weakness and strength. Attack where victory is possible, and in defense make oneself invincible; assess the distinction between surplus strength and insufficiency, and both the enemy and oneself will be clearly understood. Attack what the enemy does not defend, and defend what the enemy does not attack; first make oneself invincible and await him, and the proper balance between acting first and acting later will be attained. Attacking the enemy’s resolve is superior; attacking his cities is inferior. Preserving morale is superior; defending cities is inferior. Thus attack and defense each have their essentials. Let defense issue in attack, and let attack preserve defense; thus attack and defense serve each other. Our strategy lies hidden beneath the nine depths of the earth; suddenly we advance, and the enemy cannot trace the route of our advance. Our troops move above the nine heights of heaven; suddenly we arrive, and the enemy cannot discover whence we came. Use advantage to lure…

title: 隆慶四年貴州武舉鄉試錄
text:
之使其自至者不攻之攻也害以牽之使
其不得至者不守之守也是蓋虛以示攻
守之形敵不謂我虛也而以其實應之無
攻而敵救之無守而敵備之所謂致人而
不致於人也實以運攻守之機敵不謂我
實也而以其虛應之無救則攻必瑕矣無
備則守必堅矣所謂立於不敗之地而不
失敵之敗也彼市租擊牛者成破胡之蹟
休士謹壁者收取楚之功陳舟臨晉木罌
===
濟而魏豹虜聲擊山都阿頭破而秦豐走
魏伐趙都直走大梁而邯鄲解吴壁東南
令備西北而不得入七縱平南中者奪心
天威之語大義鼓士卒者効忠奉天之圖
所謂妙達虛實之理善措攻守之用者非
耶所謂得於方而不泥於方者非耶若霍
去病棄去不學而曰方略何如張雎陽不
依古法而使兵將相習則胸中固有孫吴
而自得於法之外者多矣雖然將爲君守
punctuated: 之，使其自至者，不攻之攻也；害以牽之，使其不得至者，不守之守也。是蓋虛以示攻守之形，敵不謂我虛也，而以其實應之；無攻而敵救之，無守而敵備之，所謂致人而不致於人也。實以運攻守之機，敵不謂我實也，而以其虛應之；無救則攻必瑕矣，無備則守必堅矣，所謂立於不敗之地而不失敵之敗也。彼市租擊牛者，成破胡之蹟；休士謹壁者，收取楚之功。陳舟臨晉，木罌濟而魏豹虜；聲擊山都，阿頭破而秦豐走。魏伐趙都，直走大梁而邯鄲解；吴壁東南，令備西北而不得入。七縱平南中者，奪心天威之語；大義鼓士卒者，効忠奉天之圖。所謂妙達虛實之理、善措攻守之用者，非耶？所謂得於方而不泥於方者，非耶？若霍去病棄去不學而曰「方略何如」，張雎陽不依古法而使兵將相習，則胸中固有孫吴，而自得於法之外者多矣。雖然，將爲君守
translation_en:
…them, causing them to come of their own accord: this is attacking without attacking. To draw them away by threatening harm, so that they cannot arrive: this is defending without defending. Here one uses emptiness to display the appearance of attack or defense; the enemy does not recognize our emptiness and responds with substantial forces. Though there is no attack, the enemy sends relief; though there is no defense, the enemy makes preparations. This is what is meant by making others come to you without being made to go to them. One uses substantial strength to put the opportunities for attack and defense into motion; the enemy does not recognize our strength and responds with emptiness. Without relief, the point attacked will surely be vulnerable; without preparations against us, our defense will surely be firm. This is what is meant by establishing oneself in an invincible position while missing no opportunity to defeat the enemy.

The one who used market revenues to slaughter oxen [?] achieved the defeat of the Hu; the one who rested his soldiers and carefully guarded his ramparts won the conquest of Chu. Boats were arrayed at Linjin, but the crossing was made with wooden jars, and Wei Bao was captured. An attack on Shandu was proclaimed, but Atou was stormed, and Qin Feng fled. When Wei attacked Zhao’s capital, a direct advance on Daliang relieved Handan. Wu encamped to the southeast; orders were given to prepare defenses to the northwest, and Wu could not break in. The one who pacified Nanzhong through seven releases won over hearts, eliciting words about his heavenly might [?]; the one who roused his soldiers with the great principles of righteousness pursued a plan of loyal service at Fengtian [?]. Were these not men who grasped with subtlety the principles of emptiness and substance and skillfully applied attack and defense? Were they not men who mastered methods without becoming bound by them?

As for Huo Qubing, who cast aside study and said, “What of strategy?” and Zhang of Suiyang, who did not follow ancient methods but made his soldiers and commanders thoroughly familiar with one another: they surely already had Sunzi and Wuzi within their hearts, and much of what they grasped for themselves lay beyond prescribed methods. Nevertheless, a general guards on behalf of his ruler …

title: 隆慶四年貴州武舉鄉試錄
text:
國者也不可有一毫邀功之念君爲國任
將者也不可有一毫好大之心戰不可忘
也亦不可好也故曰患在百里之內不與
一日之師患在千里之內不與一月之師
患在四海之內不與一歲之師而先王愼
德保邦之要固自有在矣愚敢以是終其
說
第二問
吴學易
馬上中叁箭
步下中貳箭
===
考試官知府沈　批
子能條答詳悉必胷中素有韜略宜魁多士
考試官知府李　批
具見是篇錄之
兵之資器以制敵猶醫之用藥以治病乎
故醫之所須者藥也藥之所按者方也而
所以論陰陽視毫毛十全無失者則非方
punctuated:
國者也，不可有一毫邀功之念；君爲國任將者也，不可有一毫好大之心。戰不可忘也，亦不可好也。故曰：「患在百里之內，不與一日之師；患在千里之內，不與一月之師；患在四海之內，不與一歲之師。」而先王愼德保邦之要，固自有在矣。愚敢以是終其說。
第二問
吴學易
馬上中叁箭，步下中貳箭。
考試官知府沈批：
子能條答詳悉，必胷中素有韜略，宜魁多士。
考試官知府李批：
具見是篇，錄之。
兵之資器以制敵，猶醫之用藥以治病乎？故醫之所須者藥也，藥之所按者方也，而所以論陰陽、視毫毛，十全無失者，則非方
translation_en:
…the state; he must not harbor the slightest thought of seeking personal credit. The ruler appoints generals on behalf of the state; he must not harbor the slightest desire for aggrandizement. Warfare must not be forgotten, but neither must it be cherished. Thus it is said: “When trouble lies within a hundred li, do not commit an army for a single day; when trouble lies within a thousand li, do not commit an army for a single month; when trouble lies within the Four Seas, do not commit an army for a single year.” The essential means by which the former kings attended carefully to virtue and preserved their states assuredly lay elsewhere. I venture to conclude my discussion with this.
Second Question
Wu Xueyi.
He scored three arrow hits on horseback and two on foot.
Comment by Examiner Shen, Prefect:
You have answered each point thoroughly and in detail. You must have long possessed a sound understanding of military strategy. You deserve to rank first among the candidates.
Comment by Examiner Li, Prefect:
All is evident in this essay. Include it in the record.
Is the military’s reliance on weapons to overcome the enemy like a physician’s use of medicines to cure illness? What a physician requires is medicine, and medicines are prescribed according to formulas. Yet the means of assessing yin and yang, discerning the finest details, and achieving complete success without error are not things that formulas…

title: 隆慶四年貴州武舉鄉試錄
text:
之所能盡兵之所資者器也器之所習者
法也而所以窺敵制變知彼知已循環無
端者則非法之所能拘是故制而用之謂
之法神而明之存乎人非聖儒不能深於
醫非良將不能妙於變知乎此而執事所
詢火器之用摧堅破敵之妙可識矣且夫
兵者凶器也非儒者所事火器一技也非
兵家所先而執事詢及之何也文事武備
其道相須克詰戎兵固治世所不廢者也
===
即小可以知大舉一可以知三達於用器
者固通於用兵者也吾嘗評夫庸將之論
火器也隨聲附和以謂制敵長技莫先於
此矣而豈知其有不足恃者乎不知其不
足恃則亦何以知其深可恃哉嗟夫天下
肱於名實久矣是故燕麥不可以充饑堯
漿不可以止渴兔絲不可以禦寒何也名
雖是而實則非也東南之竹箭旁枝揉曲
者不可以貫犀革荊楚之杞梓離奇液構
punctuated:
之所能盡。兵之所資者器也，器之所習者法也，而所以窺敵制變、知彼知已、循環無端者，則非法之所能拘。是故制而用之謂之法，神而明之存乎人。非聖儒不能深於醫，非良將不能妙於變。知乎此，而執事所詢火器之用、摧堅破敵之妙可識矣。且夫兵者，凶器也，非儒者所事；火器，一技也，非兵家所先。而執事詢及之，何也？文事武備，其道相須，克詰戎兵，固治世所不廢者也。即小可以知大，舉一可以知三。達於用器者，固通於用兵者也。
吾嘗評夫庸將之論火器也，隨聲附和，以謂制敵長技莫先於此矣，而豈知其有不足恃者乎？不知其不足恃，則亦何以知其深可恃哉？嗟夫！天下肱於名實久矣。是故燕麥不可以充饑，堯漿不可以止渴，兔絲不可以禦寒。何也？名雖是，而實則非也。東南之竹箭，旁枝揉曲者，不可以貫犀革；荊楚之杞梓，離奇液構
translation_en:
…cannot be fully encompassed by prescriptions. What warfare relies upon is weaponry; what governs practice with weaponry is method. Yet observing the enemy and responding to changing circumstances, knowing the enemy and oneself, and adapting in an endless cycle cannot be confined within methods. Thus, establishing something and putting it to use is called method; bringing it to life through inspired understanding rests with the person. Only a sagely scholar can attain profound understanding of medicine; only an excellent general can respond consummately to change. Once this is understood, one can comprehend the use of firearms and the subtleties of smashing strong positions and defeating the enemy about which you have inquired. Now, weapons are instruments of ill omen, not the concern of Confucian scholars; firearms constitute a single technical skill, not the foremost concern of military experts. Why, then, have you inquired about them? Civil affairs and military preparedness depend upon one another. Keeping arms in good order is certainly something that even a well-governed age does not abandon. From the small one can understand the great; from one instance one can infer three. Whoever comprehends the use of weapons surely also understands the employment of troops.
I have often considered how mediocre generals discuss firearms: they echo what others say, claiming that no technique for overcoming the enemy surpasses this one. But do they recognize that there are respects in which firearms cannot be relied upon? Without understanding where they are unreliable, how can one understand where they can be relied upon profoundly? Alas! The world has long been confused [?] about names and realities. Thus, wild oats cannot satisfy hunger, ‘Yao broth’ [?] cannot quench thirst, and dodder cannot ward off cold. Why? Although the names suggest otherwise, the actual things do not answer to them. Among the bamboos of the southeast, those with side branches and bent shafts cannot pierce rhinoceros hide; among the qi and zi timber trees of Jingchu, those that are gnarled and twisted [?] …

title: 隆慶四年貴州武舉鄉試錄
text:
者不可以備棟梁冀北之産袀攣踠跌者
不可以馳千里何也名雖存而實則亡也
今天下之眩於名實者亦多矣豈獨火器
爲然乎嗟夫安得達權審勢之士而與之
論九流哉常攷漢書載兵法技巧十二家
專言習手足便器械積機關以立攻守之
勝而皆未甞及火器也孫子之論火攻則
曰火人火積火輜火庫火隊而亦未甞及
火器也器果何所昉乎宋開寶咸平有火
毬火箭之法而用銅鐵爲器發以火藥者
則未聞也蓋其制始於近代傳於西域而
特用於今日者也故古之所謂礮者以機
發石而已宋魏勝之礮車在陣中元亦思
馬之置礮以攻城者是也其後則以火藥
爲號又其後則以銅鐵爲器然而發石之
遲重固不若火器之便利矣夫火器之用
語其洞堅及遠則强弓勁弩未之逮也而
况於前代之置礮者乎矢祚
punctuated:
者，不可以備棟梁；冀北之産，袀攣踠跌者，不可以馳千里。何也？名雖存而實則亡也。今天下之眩於名實者亦多矣，豈獨火器爲然乎？嗟夫！安得達權審勢之士，而與之論九流哉？
常攷《漢書》載兵法技巧十二家，專言習手足、便器械、積機關，以立攻守之勝，而皆未甞及火器也。《孫子》之論火攻，則曰火人、火積、火輜、火庫、火隊，而亦未甞及火器也。器果何所昉乎？宋開寶、咸平有火毬、火箭之法，而用銅鐵爲器、發以火藥者，則未聞也。蓋其制始於近代，傳於西域，而特用於今日者也。故古之所謂礮者，以機發石而已。宋魏勝之礮車在陣中，元亦思馬之置礮以攻城者，是也。其後則以火藥爲號，又其後則以銅鐵爲器。然而發石之遲重，固不若火器之便利矣。夫火器之用，語其洞堅及遠，則强弓勁弩未之逮也，而况於前代之置礮者乎？矢祚
translation_en:
…cannot serve as ridgepoles and beams; horses bred in northern Ji that are misshapen, cramped, or stumbling [?] cannot gallop a thousand li. Why? Although the name remains, the substance is gone. Today, many people throughout the realm are confused about names and realities. Surely this is not true of firearms alone! Alas! Where might one find men who understand expedient measures and assess circumstances, with whom to discuss the nine schools of thought?
I have examined the History of the Han, which records twelve schools of military techniques and skills. They speak specifically of training the hands and feet, becoming proficient with weapons and equipment, and assembling mechanical devices to secure victory in attack and defense; yet none mentions firearms. Master Sun, in discussing attacks by fire, speaks of burning men, stores, baggage trains, arsenals, and marching columns, but likewise never mentions firearms. Where, then, did these weapons originate? During the Kaibao and Xianping reign periods of the Song, there were methods involving fireballs and fire arrows, but I have heard of none involving weapons made of copper or iron and discharged with gunpowder. Their design apparently originated in recent times and was transmitted from the Western Regions, coming into particular use in our own day. Thus, what the ancients called pao were merely machines for launching stones. Such were the catapult carts that Wei Sheng of the Song deployed in his battle formations, and the catapults that Yisima of the Yuan set up to attack cities. Later, gunpowder was used for signaling; later still, copper and iron were used to make the weapons. Yet the slowness and cumbersome nature of stone-launching machines certainly fell short of the convenience of firearms. As for the utility of firearms, in penetrating hard defenses and reaching distant targets, even powerful bows and strong crossbows cannot match them. How much less could the catapults deployed in earlier ages! [The concluding characters 矢祚 are unclear: ?] …

title: 隆慶四年貴州武舉鄉試錄
text:
國家錫以自古所無之兵器五兵而淼其一
五行而用其三火器之用莫善於此矣近
者復叅以東南諸夷之制度特用中國之
智巧愈精愈便誠有如執事所云者若夫
制器之法則嘗欲其長長者所以爲遠也
不長則不能以及遠内欲其直直者所以
爲中也不直則不能以中賦而視之欲其
小大之一也不一則爽鍜而鍊之欲其厚
薄之均也不均則敝此制器之法也今之
===
制器者有一於是乎和藥者欲細取其發
之捷也不細則火力不續用器者欲習取
其藝之巧也不習則心手不應以鐵爲器
不用則易故必先試而後可用也以銅爲
器火發則易柔必得水而後可堅也此用
器之法也今之用器者果合於此乎執事
謂臨敵用器分爲三行中倍於前後倍於
中者法曰凡用火器將發敵人必伏既發
則復起故分爲三行後倍於前以待之前
punctuated:
國家錫以自古所無之兵器，五兵而淼其一，五行而用其三，火器之用莫善於此矣。近者復叅以東南諸夷之制度，特用中國之智巧，愈精愈便，誠有如執事所云者。若夫制器之法，則嘗欲其長，長者所以爲遠也，不長則不能以及遠。内欲其直，直者所以爲中也，不直則不能以中。賦而視之，欲其小大之一也，不一則爽；鍜而鍊之，欲其厚薄之均也，不均則敝。此制器之法也。今之制器者有一於是乎？

和藥者欲細，取其發之捷也，不細則火力不續；用器者欲習，取其藝之巧也，不習則心手不應。以鐵爲器，不用則易，故必先試而後可用也；以銅爲器，火發則易柔，必得水而後可堅也。此用器之法也。今之用器者果合於此乎？

執事謂臨敵用器，分爲三行，中倍於前，後倍於中者，法曰：凡用火器，將發，敵人必伏；既發，則復起。故分爲三行，後倍於前，以待之。前
translation_en:
…the state is bestowed with weapons such as have never existed since antiquity. Among the five kinds of weapons, they constitute one [?]; of the five phases, they employ three. Nothing surpasses these firearms in usefulness. Recently, the designs of the various southeastern foreign peoples have also been incorporated, with Chinese ingenuity especially brought to bear, making them ever more refined and convenient—just as you have said, sir. As for the method of making these weapons, one always wants them long: length gives them range; without length, they cannot reach far. The interior should be straight: straightness ensures accuracy; without straightness, they cannot hit the mark. In examining them [?], one wants their dimensions to be uniform; otherwise, they will go awry. In forging and refining them, one wants their thickness to be even; otherwise, they will fail. Such is the method of making these weapons. Do those who make them today meet even one of these requirements?

Those who compound the gunpowder should make it fine, to ensure swift ignition; if it is not fine, the force of the fire will not be sustained. Those who use the weapons should be practiced, to achieve skill in their art; without practice, mind and hand will not respond to each other. Weapons made of iron deteriorate [?] when unused, so they must first be tested before they can be employed. Weapons made of copper readily soften when fired and must receive water before they can become firm again. Such is the method of using these weapons. Do those who use them today truly conform to it?

Thus the men are divided into three ranks, each rearward rank twice the size of the one before it, to await them. Those in front…

title: 隆慶四年貴州武舉鄉試錄
text:
者既發敵人必伏伺其復起則後者繼之
則敵自無所遯此制勝之道也執事又謂
中陣不堅則前行無固志主將不明則雖
用無成功不盡知火器之害者不盡知火
器之利法曰凡用火器者必視中權之堅
瑕以爲勇怯兵不勇將不明則用者無固
志是以器予敵也故以堅攻瑕雖不用火
器而勝可知也以瑕攻堅雖用火器而敗
可知也若勍敵相當雌雄未決權堅破陣
===
亦孰善於火器乎此亦制勝之道也夫不
明於捍禦之法者不足以盡佐攻之妙法
曰柔能勝剛故火力之所及雖金鐵不能
支也捍禦之法剛柔相勝之用解厭之方
亦多術矣有不可以輕泄者夫不知所以
自衛則不知所以攻敵此其所當兼知者
執事又謂北虜控弦數萬行不成列火器
未及施而短兵已接刃火器不可用於北
虜者似矣然據險邀擊用奇設伏乘夜掩
punctuated:
者既發，敵人必伏，伺其復起，則後者繼之，則敵自無所遯，此制勝之道也。執事又謂：「中陣不堅，則前行無固志；主將不明，則雖用無成功；不盡知火器之害者，不盡知火器之利。」法曰：「凡用火器者，必視中權之堅瑕，以爲勇怯。兵不勇，將不明，則用者無固志，是以器予敵也。」故以堅攻瑕，雖不用火器，而勝可知也；以瑕攻堅，雖用火器，而敗可知也。若勍敵相當，雌雄未決，權堅破陣，亦孰善於火器乎？此亦制勝之道也。夫不明於捍禦之法者，不足以盡佐攻之妙。法曰：「柔能勝剛。」故火力之所及，雖金鐵不能支也。捍禦之法，剛柔相勝之用，解厭之方，亦多術矣，有不可以輕泄者。夫不知所以自衛，則不知所以攻敵，此其所當兼知者。
執事又謂：「北虜控弦數萬，行不成列，火器未及施，而短兵已接刃，火器不可用於北虜者。」似矣。然據險邀擊，用奇設伏，乘夜掩
translation_en:
…once those in front have fired, the enemy will certainly take cover. Waiting for them to rise again, those behind continue the fire, so that the enemy naturally has nowhere to escape. This is the way to secure victory. You further state: “If the central formation is not firm, the forward ranks will lack steadfast resolve; if the commanding general lacks discernment, even employing firearms will bring no success. Those who do not fully understand the disadvantages of firearms do not fully understand their advantages.” The rules say: “All who employ firearms take courage or grow fearful according to the strength or weakness of the central command. If the soldiers lack courage and the general lacks discernment, those employing them will have no steadfast resolve: this amounts to handing weapons to the enemy.” Thus, when strength attacks weakness, victory can be predicted even without firearms; when weakness attacks strength, defeat can be predicted even with firearms. But when formidable opponents are evenly matched and the outcome remains undecided, what is better than firearms for overcoming strong positions [?] and breaking formations? This too is the way to secure victory. Those who do not understand methods of defense cannot fully realize the subtle efficacy of assisting an attack. The rules say: “The yielding can overcome the hard.” Thus, wherever firepower reaches, even metal and iron cannot withstand it. Methods of defense, applications of the hard and the yielding overcoming one another, and means of counteracting suppression [?] comprise many techniques; some cannot be divulged lightly. Those who do not know how to defend themselves do not know how to attack the enemy. These are things that must be understood together.
You further state: “The northern barbarians have tens of thousands of bowmen, who move without forming ranks. Before firearms can be deployed, close-quarter weapons have already crossed blades; firearms therefore cannot be used against the northern barbarians.” This seems plausible. Yet one may occupy defensible terrain to intercept them, employ surprise tactics and lay ambushes, or take advantage of night to launch a surprise attack…

title: 隆慶四年貴州武舉鄉試錄
text:
襲在主將運用之妙何如耳奚爲其不可
哉執事又謂法令稍弛奸商互市邊徼教
習反爲彼用則火器不可習於西南者似
矣然
國初頼川西平之得志於平緬諸夷者皆用
火器以寡擊衆今欲教習以懾服諸夷則
亦惟謹關塞出入之防嚴奸商互市之禁
而已奚爲其不可習哉凡若此者法也非
所論於法之外者也法之所在可以言傳
===
可以意致法之外者言之所不能傳意之
所不能致也古者用車戰而晉人舍車爲
卒竟以成功戰必用戈矛而齊人棄矛用
劒遂以破敵制勝有機用器有時不可
以預設機不可以先圖通於此者可以用
器矣夫事有卽小可以知大者故決積水
灌雩婁者知其智之足以治國辦繁劇齊
勞佚者知其材之足以治兵然則通於火
器之法者其將略不亦可知乎雖然用心
punctuated: 襲，在主將運用之妙何如耳，奚爲其不可哉？執事又謂法令稍弛，奸商互市邊徼，教習反爲彼用，則火器不可習於西南者似矣。然國初頼川西平之得志於平緬諸夷者，皆用火器以寡擊衆。今欲教習以懾服諸夷，則亦惟謹關塞出入之防，嚴奸商互市之禁而已，奚爲其不可習哉？凡若此者，法也，非所論於法之外者也。法之所在，可以言傳，可以意致；法之外者，言之所不能傳，意之所不能致也。古者用車戰，而晉人舍車爲卒，竟以成功；戰必用戈矛，而齊人棄矛用劒，遂以破敵。制勝有機，用器有時，不可以預設，機不可以先圖。通於此者，可以用器矣。夫事有卽小可以知大者，故決積水灌雩婁者，知其智之足以治國；辦繁劇齊勞佚者，知其材之足以治兵。然則通於火器之法者，其將略不亦可知乎？雖然，用心
translation_en:
…surprise attacks: it depends simply on how skillfully the commanding general employs them. Why should this be impossible? You further say that if laws and orders become somewhat lax, unscrupulous merchants will trade along the frontier, and the training will instead be put to use by the enemy. It thus seems plausible that firearms should not be taught and practiced in the southwest. Yet at the founding of the dynasty, the successes of Chuan Xiping [?] in pacifying the various non-Chinese peoples of Mian were all achieved by using firearms to strike larger forces with smaller ones. If we now wish to conduct training to overawe and subdue these peoples, we need only guard passage through the frontier barriers carefully and strictly enforce the prohibition on illicit trade by unscrupulous merchants. Why should such training be impossible?

All these things concern methods; they are not what is meant by that which lies beyond methods. What belongs to methods can be transmitted in words and grasped in thought. What lies beyond methods cannot be transmitted in words or reached through thought. In antiquity, battles were fought with chariots, yet the men of Jin abandoned their chariots to become foot soldiers and ultimately succeeded. Battles required dagger-axes and spears, yet the men of Qi discarded their spears and used swords, thereby defeating the enemy. Victory depends on an opportunity, and weapons have their proper moment of use. This cannot be fixed beforehand, nor can the opportunity be planned in advance. Those who understand this can employ weapons.

Can we not, then, likewise discern the generalship of someone who thoroughly understands the methods of firearms? Nevertheless, in applying one's mind…

title: 隆慶四年貴州武舉鄉試錄
text:
戒於忍擇術貴於慎佳兵不祥之器以是
傳受教習毋乃傷於仁乎曰仁者愛人故
惡人之害之也故除殘去暴仁者之事也
行一不義殺一不辜而有所不爲仁者之
心也有仁者之心雖殺人皆仁也縠蔌以
養人藥石以去病其於生人一也疾醫之
用烏附瘍醫之用劀殺五毒此豈不仁者
哉若無仁者之心而從事於不祥之器則
君子不由也
===
論
人君有必勝之道
蘇九野
馬上中捌箭
步下中貳箭
考試官知府沈 批〔王道以得民心爲本未聞勝之也〕
〔況於必勝之乎觀子議論直瀉胷中定見尉繚子不足語此佳士〕
考試官知府李 批〔議論純正是知治天下之要〕
punctuated:
戒於忍，擇術貴於慎。佳兵，不祥之器，以是傳受教習，毋乃傷於仁乎？曰：仁者愛人，故惡人之害之也。故除殘去暴，仁者之事也；行一不義，殺一不辜，而有所不爲，仁者之心也。有仁者之心，雖殺人，皆仁也。縠蔌以養人，藥石以去病，其於生人一也。疾醫之用烏附，瘍醫之用劀殺五毒，此豈不仁者哉？若無仁者之心，而從事於不祥之器，則君子不由也。

論
人君有必勝之道
蘇九野
馬上中捌箭，步下中貳箭。
考試官知府沈批〔王道以得民心爲本，未聞勝之也。〕〔況於必勝之乎？觀子議論，直瀉胷中定見，尉繚子不足語此，佳士！〕
考試官知府李批〔議論純正，是知治天下之要。〕
translation_en:
…one must guard against cruelty in one’s intentions and exercise care in choosing one’s arts. Fine weapons are inauspicious instruments. Would transmitting and teaching their use not impair benevolence? The reply is: A benevolent person loves others and therefore abhors anyone’s harming them. Thus, eliminating the cruel and removing the violent are the deeds of a benevolent person. Refusing to commit even one unrighteous act or kill even one innocent person manifests a benevolent heart. With a benevolent heart, even killing can be benevolent. Grain and vegetables [?] nourish people; medicines remove illness: they are alike in sustaining human life. Physicians use aconite preparations, and surgeons use scraping, removal of diseased tissue, and the five toxic drugs. Does this make them unbenevolent? But to employ inauspicious instruments without a benevolent heart is a course the gentleman will not follow.

Discourse
“The Ruler Has a Way to Ensure Victory”
Su Jiuye
He scored eight arrow hits on horseback and two on foot.

Comment by Examiner Shen, Prefect: 〔The kingly Way rests on winning the people’s hearts; I have never heard of overcoming them.〕〔How much less of ensuring victory over them! Reading your argument, I see firmly held convictions pouring straight from your breast. The Weiliaozi is inadequate to discuss this. An excellent scholar!〕

Comment by Examiner Li, Prefect: 〔The argument is sound and orthodox: this shows an understanding of the essentials of governing all under Heaven.〕

title: 隆慶四年貴州武舉鄉試錄
text:
人君統天下而無外而曰有必勝之道者其起
於世之衰乎夫世治則天下皆吾統而無外也
無外則無爭而何有於勝之名自天下之角立
者起而於是乎有爭爭斯有勝之名而世之曰
尋於干戈也烈矣然則有必勝之道者有必然
之患者也勝在於君患貽其民而勝豈人君之
所樂有也哉故曰人君有必勝之道蓋起於世
之衰而非所以語夫大順大化之極也歟竊觀
夫聖王之御寓内也至仁以覆燾之如化育包
===
涵而民自戴於上也則無用以道勝之使不離
焉至義以整裁之如化育嚴凝而民自畏於上
也則無用以道勝之使不叛焉至禮以品節之
如化育經緯而民自順於上也則無用以道勝
之使不悖焉至智以照臨之如化育貞觀而民
自孚於上也則無用以道勝之使不欺焉蓋聖
人之勝天下也以無心感之而默運其漸摩之
化有勝之理無勝之制也天下之勝於聖人也
以無心應之而潛孚其鼓舞之神有勝之効無
punctuated:
人君統天下而無外，而曰有必勝之道者，其起於世之衰乎？夫世治，則天下皆吾統而無外也。無外則無爭，而何有於勝之名？自天下之角立者起，而於是乎有爭，爭斯有勝之名，而世之曰尋於干戈也烈矣。然則有必勝之道者，有必然之患者也。勝在於君，患貽其民，而勝豈人君之所樂有也哉？故曰「人君有必勝之道」，蓋起於世之衰，而非所以語夫大順大化之極也歟？

The ruler governs all under Heaven, with nothing outside his domain. Did the claim that he possesses a way to certain victory arise, then, from the decline of the age? When the world is well governed, all under Heaven falls within his rule, with nothing outside it. With nothing outside, there is no contention; how, then, could there even be the name of victory? Once rival powers arise under Heaven, contention begins. With contention comes the name of victory, and the world’s daily recourse to arms [?] grows fierce indeed. Thus, to possess a way to certain victory is also to possess a source of inevitable calamity. Victory belongs to the ruler, but calamity is bequeathed to his people. How could victory be something a ruler delights in possessing? Hence the saying, “The ruler possesses a way to certain victory,” surely arose from the decline of the age. It is hardly language suited to the utmost perfection of great harmony and great transformation, is it?

I humbly observe that when the sage-kings governed the realm, they sheltered it with consummate benevolence, like the all-embracing nurture of nature. They ordered and regulated the realm with consummate righteousness, like the stern, congealing power of nature’s transformations. The people spontaneously stood in awe of their ruler, so there was no need to employ a method of prevailing over them to keep them from rebelling. They established distinctions and measures through consummate ritual propriety, like the ordering pattern of nature’s transformations. 古矣治日衰矣是故仁不足以懷而離者衆於
是思以勝其離之民焉而連結之術用矣義不

擊斷之術用矣禮不足以齊而悖者衆於是思
以勝其悖之民焉而操切之術用矣智不足以
照而欺者衆於是思以勝其欺之民焉而鉤抉
之術用矣人見夫連結行而民不離則謂以連
結勝而不知民未始有戴上之心也人見夫擊

則惡在其爲必勝之道也哉彼尉繚子者當夫
戰攻之世習於傾變之權而曰連刑全軍全曲
punctuated: 勝之迹也。此大順大化，治之極也。降是而時不古矣，治日衰矣。是故仁不足以懷，而離者衆，於是思以勝其離之民焉，而連結之術用矣；義不足以正，而叛者衆，於是思以勝其叛之民焉，而擊斷之術用矣；禮不足以齊，而悖者衆，於是思以勝其悖之民焉，而操切之術用矣；智不足以照，而欺者衆，於是思以勝其欺之民焉，而鉤抉之術用矣。人見夫連結行而民不離，則謂以連結勝，而不知民未始有戴上之心也；人見夫擊斷行而民不叛，則謂以擊斷勝，而不知民未始有畏上之心也；人見夫操切行而民不悖，則謂以操切勝，而不知民未始有順上之心也；人見夫鉤抉行而民不欺，則謂以鉤抉勝，而不知民未始有孚上之心也。夫未嘗戴之，則有時而離之矣；未嘗畏之，則有時而叛之矣；未嘗順之，則有時而悖之矣；未嘗孚之，則有時而欺之矣。然則惡在其爲必勝之道也哉？彼尉繚子者，當夫戰攻之世，習於傾變之權，而曰連刑、全軍、全曲
translation_en:
…traces of being prevailed over. Such perfect compliance and profound transformation constitute the highest achievement of government. Below this level, the times no longer resemble antiquity, and government declines daily. Thus, when benevolence is insufficient to win people’s hearts and many become estranged, rulers seek to prevail over their estranged subjects, and techniques of binding people together come into use. When righteousness is insufficient to set people right and many rebel, rulers seek to prevail over their rebellious subjects, and techniques of punitive suppression come into use. When ritual propriety is insufficient to bring people into order and many become defiant, rulers seek to prevail over their defiant subjects, and techniques of harsh coercion come into use. When wisdom is insufficient to discern matters and many practise deception, rulers seek to prevail over their deceitful subjects, and techniques of probing and exposure come into use.

People see that, when bonds are imposed, the populace does not become estranged, and say that these bonds have prevailed; they do not realize that the people have never felt any inclination to uphold their ruler. They see that, when punitive suppression is practised, the populace does not rebel, and say that suppression has prevailed; they do not realize that the people have never felt any awe of their ruler. They see that, when harsh coercion is practised, the populace does not act defiantly, and say that coercion has prevailed; they do not realize that the people have never felt any inclination to obey their ruler. They see that, when probing and exposure are practised, the populace does not deceive, and say that these techniques have prevailed; they do not realize that the people have never felt any trust in their ruler.

If they have never upheld him, a time will come when they abandon him. If they have never stood in awe of him, a time will come when they rebel against him. If they have never obeyed him, a time will come when they defy him. If they have never trusted him, a time will come when they deceive him. How, then, can these techniques constitute a way of invariably prevailing?

That Master Wei Liao lived in an age of warfare and attack and was versed in expedients of subversion and shifting stratagems. He spoke of linked punishments, preserving the army intact, and preserving its units intact…

title: 隆慶四年貴州武舉鄉試錄
text:
則連結是已曰地禁死士力卒則擊斷是已曰
開塞金鼓陳車則操切是已曰分限號別玉章
則鉤校是已蓋莫非擒殺之方而戰鬬之務也
謂足以治衆守大而不知非君子保邦之要道
也謂足以尊主顯功而不知非先王効忠之大
節也嗚呼旌旗野豎屍塡巨港之岸組練川廻
血滿長城之窟此獨非戰也哉是故舜以干羽
勝苗未聞以戰也湯以寛仁勝夏未聞以戰也
武以過劉勝殷未聞以戰也故曰善爲國者不
師善師者不陳善陳者不戰國車不出於閫組
甲不出於橐而畏服天下者非戰之謂也雖然
彼尨未賭夫必勝之害也胡亥必勝於忠諫而
望夷刼漢武必勝於土木而海内虛巡遊勝者
遍天涯之錦柔曼勝者悲斜谷之鈴詞賦勝者
庭草見危書翰勝者拙筆僅免甚矣人君之無
以必勝天下爲也書曰匹夫匹婦能勝予蓋古
帝王之用心如此尉繚子之言其未聞道也夫
punctuated:
則連結是已；曰地禁、死士、力卒，則擊斷是已；曰開塞、金鼓、陳車，則操切是已；曰分限、號別、玉章，則鉤校是已。蓋莫非擒殺之方，而戰鬬之務也。謂足以治衆守大，而不知非君子保邦之要道也；謂足以尊主顯功，而不知非先王効忠之大節也。
嗚呼！旌旗野豎，屍塡巨港之岸；組練川廻，血滿長城之窟。此獨非戰也哉？是故舜以干羽勝苗，未聞以戰也；湯以寛仁勝夏，未聞以戰也；武以過劉勝殷，未聞以戰也。故曰：「善爲國者不師，善師者不陳，善陳者不戰。」國車不出於閫，組甲不出於橐，而畏服天下者，非戰之謂也。
雖然，彼尨未賭夫必勝之害也。胡亥必勝於忠諫，而望夷刼；漢武必勝於土木，而海内虛。巡遊勝者，遍天涯之錦；柔曼勝者，悲斜谷之鈴；詞賦勝者，庭草見危；書翰勝者，拙筆僅免。甚矣，人君之無以必勝天下爲也！書曰：「匹夫匹婦能勝予。」蓋古帝王之用心如此。尉繚子之言，其未聞道也夫！
translation_en:
…then this is merely binding men together; when he speaks of restrictions on terrain, warriors prepared to die, and vigorous soldiers, this is merely striking and breaking; when he speaks of opening and blocking routes, gongs and drums, and arraying chariots, this is merely coercive control; when he speaks of divisions and boundaries, distinguishing signals, and jade insignia [?], this is merely probing and checking. These are all methods of capture and killing, all concerned with warfare. He claims that they suffice to govern the multitude and preserve a great realm, without realizing that they are not the essential Way by which a gentleman safeguards his state. He claims that they suffice to exalt the ruler and make achievements manifest, without realizing that they are not the great principles of loyal service exemplified by the former kings.
Alas! Banners stand in the wilderness, and corpses fill the banks of great waterways; ranks of armored troops wind like rivers, and blood fills the hollows of the Great Wall. Is this not precisely warfare? Thus Shun overcame the Miao with shields and feather plumes; we have never heard that he did so through warfare. Tang overcame the Xia through generosity and benevolence; we have never heard that he did so through warfare. King Wu overcame the Yin through “passing and killing” [?]; we have never heard that he did so through warfare. Hence the saying: “One skilled in governing a state does not mobilize an army; one skilled in commanding an army does not draw up battle formations; one skilled in drawing up battle formations does not fight.” To inspire awe and submission throughout the world without sending the state’s chariots beyond the gates or taking its cord-bound armor out of storage—this is what is meant by dispensing with warfare.
Even so, he has not yet witnessed [?] the harm caused by insisting on victory. Hu Hai insisted on prevailing over loyal remonstrance, only to suffer violence at Wangyi Palace. Emperor Wu of the Han insisted on prevailing in construction projects, only to impoverish the realm. The ruler who sought supremacy in imperial tours spread brocade to the ends of the earth; the ruler who sought supremacy in sensual delights grieved at the bells of Xie Valley. The ruler who sought supremacy in literary composition encountered peril over courtyard grass [?]; the ruler who sought supremacy in calligraphy barely escaped through clumsy brushwork [?]. How utterly pointless it is for a ruler to insist on prevailing over everyone under Heaven! The Book of Documents says: “An ordinary man or woman can surpass me.” Such was the disposition of the ancient emperors and kings. Judging by his words, Weiliaozi had surely never heard the Way!

title: 隆慶四年貴州武舉鄉試錄
text:
貴州武舉錄後序
隆慶庚午侍御蔡公按黔中
秋八月集文士試之矣廼其
心則切切然卽欲得士如周
召者爲
國家用也冬十月集武士試之
矣廼其心則又切切然卽欲
===
得士如方虎者爲
國家用也余曰我
朝經制荒徼所以宣布其聲敎
者旣與中州同而搜羅武略
所以品飾其條貫者亦與文
科相埒云自今言之諸衛冑
及良家子有材略者竝隸學
punctuated:
貴州武舉錄後序

隆慶庚午，侍御蔡公按黔中，秋八月集文士試之矣。廼其心則切切然，卽欲得士如周召者爲國家用也。冬十月集武士試之矣，廼其心則又切切然，卽欲得士如方虎者爲國家用也。余曰：我朝經制荒徼，所以宣布其聲敎者，旣與中州同；而搜羅武略，所以品飾其條貫者，亦與文科相埒云。自今言之，諸衛冑及良家子有材略者，竝隸學
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guizhou Military Provincial Examination

In the gengwu year of Longqing [1570], Censor Cai inspected Guizhou. In autumn, in the eighth month, he assembled the civil candidates and examined them. His earnest desire was to obtain men like the Dukes of Zhou and Shao for service to the state. In winter, in the tenth month, he assembled the military candidates and examined them. Again, his earnest desire was to obtain men like Fang Shu and Shao Hu for service to the state.

I say: in administering these remote frontiers, our dynasty disseminates its authority and moral instruction just as it does in the Central Plains. In seeking out men of military ability, it has likewise ordered and refined its examination procedures to stand on a par with the civil examinations. Speaking of present arrangements, descendants of the military guards and sons of respectable families who possess talent and strategic ability are all enrolled in schools…

title: 隆慶四年貴州武舉鄉試錄
text:
官以時督其程課而上下之
與弟子員無異蓋儲養同矣
三歲一省試初騎射再步射
三策論糊名易書一倣賓興
之制蓋選舉同矣章縫鉛槧
之士由南宮而歷卿佐馳駟
拾決之夫升司馬而建高牙
蓋任用同矣然則合遠邇爲
===
一體者非以廓其綏懷之化
而視文武爲一道者非以神
其振作之權歟至綜其行事
則廉墨檢肆正邪之歸每每
不同何歟豈上固以竝用之
術施之而士之所以自持者
punctuated: 官以時督其程課而上下之，與弟子員無異，蓋儲養同矣。三歲一省試，初騎射，再步射，三策論，糊名易書，一倣賓興之制，蓋選舉同矣。章縫鉛槧之士，由南宮而歷卿佐；馳駟拾決之夫，升司馬而建高牙，蓋任用同矣。然則合遠邇爲一體者，非以廓其綏懷之化，而視文武爲一道者，非以神其振作之權歟？至綜其行事，則廉墨、檢肆、正邪之歸，每每不同，何歟？豈上固以竝用之術施之，而士之所以自持者……
translation_en: …officials regularly supervise their prescribed studies and grade them, just as they do registered students: thus their preparation and cultivation are the same. Every three years a Provincial Examination is held: first mounted archery, then archery on foot, and third policy essays and discourses. Candidates’ names are concealed and their scripts recopied, all following the system for selecting worthy men: thus their selection is the same. Scholars wearing scholarly caps and wielding writing tools pass through the Ministry of Rites examinations and advance through posts as ministers and their assistants; men who drive teams of horses and wear archers’ armguards and thumb rings rise to become Ministers of War and erect lofty command banners: thus their employment is the same. Is not the unification of distant and nearby regions intended to extend the transforming influence that pacifies and wins allegiance? And is not treating civil and military pursuits as one way intended to give wondrous efficacy to the power of inspiring effort? Yet when their conduct is examined as a whole, why do they so often diverge toward integrity or corruption, restraint or license, uprightness or depravity? Could it be that those above indeed apply a method of employing both together, yet as for the standards by which these men govern themselves…

title: 隆慶四年貴州武舉鄉試錄
text:
武迺不逮於文歟蓋彼見夫
業屠繒者之與炎祚而不知
敦詩說禮之克匡晉烈也彼
見夫戲蹋鞠者之封居胥而
不知雅歌投壷之照燿雲臺
也彼見夫戮驂駙者之拓封
內而不知輕裘緩帶之遺思
===
峴首也彼見夫刃齊女者之
却秦師而不知匍匐歸喪之
獨忠宋室也是故射礼穿楊
非無技也而尚其廉以廉用
者貪功有不爲矣超距投石
非無勇也而尚其檢以檢出
者矯制有不爲矣開闔變化
punctuated: 武迺不逮於文歟？蓋彼見夫業屠繒者之與炎祚，而不知敦詩說禮之克匡晉烈也；彼見夫戲蹋鞠者之封居胥，而不知雅歌投壷之照燿雲臺也；彼見夫戮驂駙者之拓封內，而不知輕裘緩帶之遺思峴首也；彼見夫刃齊女者之却秦師，而不知匍匐歸喪之獨忠宋室也。是故射礼穿楊，非無技也，而尚其廉，以廉用者，貪功有不爲矣；超距投石，非無勇也，而尚其檢，以檢出者，矯制有不爲矣；開闔變化
translation_en:
…do military men then fall short of civil men? They see how men who worked as butchers and silk dealers helped establish the Han dynasty, but do not know how devotion to the Odes and exposition of the Rites could uphold the glorious achievements of Jin. They see how a man who amused himself playing kickball performed the sacrificial rite on Mount Juxu, but do not know how refined singing and pitch-pot illuminated the Cloud Terrace. They see how a man who executed an attendant charioteer [?] expanded his territory, but do not know how one who wore light furs and a loosely fastened sash left an affectionate memory at Xianshou. They see how a man who slew a woman of Qi repelled the Qin army [?], but do not know how one who hurried home to mourn displayed singular loyalty to the Song ruling house.

Thus, ritual archery and piercing a willow leaf with an arrow certainly require skill; yet integrity is what is prized, for those who exercise their abilities with integrity will refrain from certain acts done out of greed for military distinction. Leaping distances and throwing stones certainly require courage; yet restraint is what is prized, for those who take the field with restraint will refrain from falsely invoking imperial commands. Opening and closing, changing and transforming…

title: 隆慶四年貴州武舉鄉試錄
text:
難知如陰非無謀也而尚其
正以正運者詭道有不爲矣
此上將之務社稷之衛也而
何莫不本於心之忠余竊觀
太史公忻慕李將軍者至矣
至稱其爲人則曰悛悛口不
能道辭忠心信於士大夫而
===
他材勇畧不一及焉嗚呼是
可以識將之所重者端有在
矣諸士而欲爲方叔召虎以
副侍御公之望也其尚知所
師法哉昔以文舉者余得以
義規之而期其終矣兹以武
舉者余又得以義規之而期
punctuated: 難知如陰，非無謀也，而尚其正；以正運者，詭道有不爲矣。此上將之務，社稷之衛也，而何莫不本於心之忠？余竊觀太史公忻慕李將軍者至矣，至稱其爲人，則曰：「悛悛，口不能道辭，忠心信於士大夫。」而他材勇畧，不一及焉。嗚呼！是可以識將之所重者，端有在矣。諸士而欲爲方叔、召虎，以副侍御公之望也，其尚知所師法哉！昔以文舉者，余得以義規之，而期其終矣。兹以武舉者，余又得以義規之，而期
translation_en:
…as hard to discern as darkness: this is not to lack strategic resourcefulness, yet uprightness is prized. Those who conduct operations with uprightness will refrain from certain forms of deception. These are the duties of a supreme commander and the safeguards of the state. How could any of them fail to be rooted in loyalty of heart?

I observe that the Grand Historian’s admiration for General Li was profound. Yet when describing his character, he said: “Unassuming [?], he could not express himself eloquently; his loyal heart was trusted by the scholar-officials.” He did not mention a single one of his other talents, feats of courage, or strategies. Alas! From this we can recognize that there is indeed a particular foundation for what matters most in a commander.

If you gentlemen wish to become men like Fang Shu and Shao Hu, fulfilling the expectations of His Honor the Censor, may you understand whom to take as your models! Previously, I was able to admonish those selected through the civil examination in accordance with righteousness, hoping that they would uphold it to the end. Now, for those selected through the military examination, I can again admonish them in accordance with righteousness, and hope…

title: 隆慶四年貴州武舉鄉試錄
text:
其終如此云
貴州等處提刑按察司副使
秦淦謹序
punctuated:
其終如此云。
貴州等處提刑按察司副使秦淦謹序。
translation_en:
…their ultimate accomplishment: such are my words.
Qin Gan, Vice Commissioner of the Guizhou Provincial Surveillance Commission, respectfully composed this preface.
